source.title: Learning When to Trust Which Teacher for Weakly Supervised ASR
source.authors: Aakriti Agrawal; M. Rao; Anit Kumar Sahu; Gopinath Chennupati; A. Stolcke

page_placements.theme: Strong-to-weak and same-size distillation: a student that is smaller than or equal to its teacher sometimes exceeds it

record.tranche_reason: The study trains ASR students from scratch on transcripts from weaker expert models and compares student WER with teacher WER. This conceptually tests whether a student can outperform its weak supervisor, but it uses multiple teachers and does not calculate PGR.
record.gate_note: Table 5 and Table 6 evaluate the Smart-Weighter's expert-selection accuracy and weighted WER, not the student's weak-to-strong task performance, so they are not rows. The Oracle results in Table 4 are omitted; the student-method comparisons are retained.
record.test_reason: Not a weak-to-strong test. The 60M RNN-T student has the same size and architecture as the three 60M RNN-T teachers. It is trained from scratch on pseudo-labels, so no supervisor–student capability gap exists. Gains come from more audio (10K h LibriLight, or all of LibriSpeech, versus about 320 h per expert) and from combining several teachers. There is no strong-model ceiling and no PGR. This is same-capacity multi-teacher self-training, a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that Smart-Weighter-weighted multi-expert training gives a 4–25% improvement over uniform weighting, single best expert and ROVER. However, Table 4 Random TestOther shows no gain over All-Experts (18.93 vs 18.86), despite the authors' claim of statistically significant improvement in all settings. The entropy feature improves the weighter's selection accuracy (Table 6), not student WER.
record.recipe_differences: The students are trained from scratch on ASR transcripts from multiple same-size RNN-T experts, with a learned utterance-level weighter or other teacher-combination baselines. The study does not fine-tune a strong pretrained model using one weaker supervisor or report PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ between Random and Clustered expert partitions and between LibriLight and LibriSpeech student-training data; Smart-Weighter does not beat All-Experts on Random TestOther in Table 4.

fits_no_version.finding: A same-size (60M) RNN-T student trained from scratch on pseudo-labels from a single same-size expert beats that expert on test WER. Test-Clean: 10.03 vs 10.82 (Random) and 9.40 vs 11.27 (Clustered). Combining multiple teachers lowers student WER further.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In same-capacity ASR self-training, a student trained on more unlabeled audio with one or more teachers' pseudo-labels can surpass its teachers (student-exceeds-teacher without a capability gap).

record.problems: The study does not report PGR or a strong-model true-label ceiling, and its students are trained from scratch rather than described as pretrained. It states that improvements are statistically significant but provides no uncertainty values or significance-test details in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 and Table 4 Train, DevClean, and DevOther student WER results are omitted to prioritize the TestClean and TestOther comparisons; Table 4 Oracle rows are also omitted. Table 2 expert results were used only as baselines for Best-Expert rows.

untested.parts: No student stronger than its supervisor, no strong ceiling, no PGR.
No weak-to-strong method gain measured as PGR.
Speech only and not a weak-to-strong setup; no vision.

record.verdict_notes: Key facts: teachers and student are all 60M RNN-Ts, and the student is trained from scratch. The student beating its teacher is attributable to more training audio and teacher combination, not to a stronger student. The Smart-Weighter uses ground-truth transcripts for 100 h. The ROVER numbers in Table 4 repeat those in Table 3. The text says 'ROVER outperforms the best teacher' by reference to Table 6, which is a weighter-accuracy table, so the reference looks wrong. No uncertainty values or significance-test details are given.

versions.untested_parts: No PGR or strong ceiling is reported. The student is trained from scratch, not described as a strong pretrained model; the setup uses multiple experts as well as a single best-expert baseline.
The study compares expert weighting and transcript-combination methods, but does not test auxiliary confidence loss or the listed loss variants, and does not calculate PGR.
No PGR sweep by supervisor or student size, no cross-task comparison, and no analysis of representations predicting PGR.
No analysis of unchecked capabilities, distribution shift, or error similarity between weak and strong models.
No theory of conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor.

tranche.reason: Same-size RNN-T students trained from scratch on expert transcripts neither test nor use the claimed generalization from weaker supervisors to stronger pretrained students.

source_check.notes: All listed values, baselines, subjects and conditions match the text; all row states should be cannot_determine for versions=none. Same model size alone does not prove equal capability, but this study establishes no stronger pretrained student; Table 4 also shows Smart-Weighter losing to All-Experts on Random TestOther (18.93 versus 18.86).
